_what_this_is: A DELIBERATELY DEFECTIVE binding set. `pass_proven` must reject it, and must
name every rule it breaks. `contract-check.py --selftest` runs the real
`pass_proven()` against this file and the fixtures beside it, and fails if any
expected finding code is missing.
One wrong way per rule, so a rule that stops working cannot hide behind another
rule still firing - which is the exact defect the whole PROVEN pass was written
to close, and it applies to the pass itself.
P0_MALFORMED           C9 reason 4 declares no mechanism
P1_NO_BINDING          C1-strawman is on disk with no entry here
P2_COUNT               C2-strawman declares two reasons, this binds one
P3_CLAIM_DRIFT         C9 reason 1's claim is not in the reason
P4_UNDEMONSTRATED      C9 reason 2 claims an enum that does not fire
P4_UNENFORCED_STALE    C9 reason 5 is recorded unenforced and its would_be fires
P5_DUPLICATE_EVIDENCE  C9 reason 3 claims reason 0's triple verbatim
P6_EXTERNAL_MISSING    C9 reason 6 names a reader code that never fires
P6_EXTERNAL_STALE      C9 reason 7 records E_SCHEMA not_reachable while it fires
P7_UNEXPLAINED         two real C9 errors are claimed by nothing
P7_UNEXPLAINED_STALE   one recorded unexplained error does not fire
P8_ORPHAN              an entry names a fixture that is not on disk
The one thing that must NOT be reported is C9 reason 0, which is bound
correctly. A checker that flags everything is as useless as one that flags
nothing, so the selftest asserts reason 0 is quiet.

recorded unenforced with a would_be triple that does fire

external.why: A false escape. E_SCHEMA fires on this body every single run.

unexplained_errors.why: A STALE RECORD. No such error is produced, so this line excuses nothing and reads as coverage.
